subject: Two charts, same x-axis, but different geoms

messages.author: b5cbe02d295306d7
messages.subject: Two charts, same x-axis, but different geoms
parts:
A while ago Hadley suggested some code to get two charts on the same x-
axis, but with different geoms. It worked a treat - but now doesnt.
I get a variety of error messages depending on different
applications. The example below gives

"Error in Ops.Date((x - from[1]), diff(from)) : / not defined for
Date objects".

I am using R2.9.0 with the most recent version of ggplot2

Very grateful for any help

simeon
+++++++++++++++++++++++++

library(ggplot2)
upper <- with(economics, data.frame(
date,
value = psavert,
position = "upper"
))

lower <- with(economics, data.frame(
date,
value = unemploy,
position = "lower"
))

ggplot(mapping = aes(date, value)) +
geom_line(data = upper) +
geom_area(data = lower) +
facet_wrap(~ position, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1)

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Two charts, same x-axis, but different geoms
parts:
Hi Simeon,

Because you are not supplying an overall data frame in the ggplot()
call, but you are supplying aesthetics, ggplot2 gets confused and
doesn't know to automatically add a date axis. Doing it yourself
fixes the problem:

ggplot(mapping = aes(date, value)) +
geom_line(data = upper) +
geom_area(data = lower) +
